headline: Argentina vs England: Mac Allister urges team to channel Maradona spirit
summary: Ahead of the World Cup semifinal in Atlanta, Alexis Mac Allister looks to the legacy of Diego Maradona to inspire Argentina's quest for a second straight final.
details: Argentina's Alexis Mac Allister has called on his teammates to draw inspiration from the legendary Diego Maradona as they prepare to face England in the World Cup semifinal on Thursday.
The high-stakes clash in Atlanta renews a historic rivalry that peaked during the 1986 World Cup, where Maradona scored two iconic goals in the quarterfinal against England.
Mac Allister, whose father Carlos played alongside Maradona, noted that he has been watching videos of the 1986 game to remember the spirit and impact of the legend.
The midfielder believes that while Maradona's unique genius was nearly impossible to replicate, Lionel Messi remains the only player capable of doing something similar.
This match marks the first World Cup meeting between the two nations since 2002, with Argentina aiming for a third final in four tournaments.
Regarding their opponents, Mac Allister stated that England is a great team that deserves respect, though he noted they have not yet played with 'Premier League intensity' in the tournament.
He expects the upcoming game to be played with high intensity and significant nerves on both sides as they fight for a spot in the final.
caption:
Can Argentina channel the spirit of Maradona to defeat England? 🇦🇷🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿

Argentina's Alexis Mac Allister has called on his teammates to draw inspiration from the legendary Diego Maradona as they prepare to face England in the World Cup semifinal on Thursday.

The high-stakes clash in Atlanta renews a historic rivalry that peaked during the 1986 World Cup, where Maradona scored two iconic goals in the quarterfinal against England.

Mac Allister, whose father Carlos played alongside Maradona, noted that he has been watching videos of the 1986 game to remember the spirit and impact of the legend.

The midfielder believes that while Maradona's unique genius was nearly impossible to replicate, Lionel Messi remains the only player capable of doing something similar.

This match marks the first World Cup meeting between the two nations since 2002, with Argentina aiming for a third final in four tournaments.

Regarding their opponents, Mac Allister stated that England is a great team that deserves respect, though he noted they have not yet played with 'Premier League intensity' in the tournament.

He expects the upcoming game to be played with high intensity and significant nerves on both sides as they fight for a spot in the final.

headline: Trump calls Iran  'Islamic Republic of Japan'  in series of public gaffes
summary: The US President has made several high-profile mistakes in recent speeches, including confusing names of world leaders and officials.
details: During a NATO summit in Turkey, Donald Trump referred to Iran as the 'Islamic Republic of Japan' while discussing a missile attack on US aircraft carriers.
In the same 10-minute window, he mistakenly asked if reporters had questions for President Putin, despite sitting next to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
The gaffes continued at another event where he called SBA head Kelly Loeffler up as 'Nicki Minaj' twice, confusing the official with the same-named American singer.
While inspecting a renovated Air Force One, Trump initially called Elon Musk 'Leon' when discussing Starlink communication technology.
These incidents have come under scrutiny as Trump has a history of mocking his political rivals, such as Joe Biden and Barack Obama, for similar verbal slips.
Critics argue that the pattern of frequent mistakes in public addresses is becoming a more common occurrence for the US President.
caption:
From 'Islamic Republic of Japan' to calling an official 'Nicki Minaj'—Donald Trump's recent verbal slips are sparking debate.

During a NATO summit in Turkey, Donald Trump referred to Iran as the 'Islamic Republic of Japan' while discussing a missile attack on US aircraft carriers.

In the same 10-minute window, he mistakenly asked if reporters had questions for President Putin, despite sitting next to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

The gaffes continued at another event where he called SBA head Kelly Loeffler up as 'Nicki Minaj' twice, confusing the official with the same-named American singer.

While inspecting a renovated Air Force One, Trump initially called Elon Musk 'Leon' when discussing Starlink communication technology.

These incidents have come under scrutiny as Trump has a history of mocking his political rivals, such as Joe Biden and Barack Obama, for similar verbal slips.

Critics argue that the pattern of frequent mistakes in public addresses is becoming a more common occurrence for the US President.
